title: Proof of Work as a life principle
tweets:
Bitcoin's consensus mechanism is called Proof of Work.

The block is either valid or it isn't. You either did the work or you didn't. The network doesn't accept approximations.

I've started applying that standard to everything else. 🧵

Proof of work is unforgeable.

You can fake a credential. You can fake confidence. You can fake a LinkedIn title.

You cannot fake the result of actual work. The output either meets the standard or it doesn't. The chain either accepts it or rejects it.

Most of modern life is built on proxies.

Degrees instead of knowledge. Titles instead of skill. Appearances instead of substance.

We've built a civilization that rewards the signal of work rather than the work itself. Most people never notice the difference.

When you internalize proof of work as a personal standard, the question changes.

Not "how do I look?" but "what did I actually build?"
Not "do people believe me?" but "is it true?"
Not "can I fake it?" but "have I earned it?"

Most people don't want this standard.

Because it removes every excuse. You can't blame the algorithm, the market, the timing, or your circumstances.

Either you did the work or you didn't. The network is indifferent to your reasons.

That indifference is the point.

Bitcoin doesn't care about your story. It validates the work.

Apply that to how you build your body, your skills, your word, your life — and you stop optimizing for appearance and start producing something real.
